observation.visible_scene: A handheld kitchen shot shows a black saucepan on a gas stove burner, filled with a light-brown frothy liquid (tea/coffee-like), against a white tiled backsplash. A person's right hand grips the handle of a white ceramic mug decorated with black polka dots and a pink band near its base. The mug is held just to the right of and above the pot for the whole excerpt.
visible_changes: The mug is gradually tilted/rotated in the hand: early frames show its side (dots and pink band facing the camera, opening turned away), and over the sequence the rim tips back until the empty white interior becomes fully visible (clearest around the middle-to-late frames), then the tilt eases slightly toward the end.
The mug's position relative to the pot stays roughly constant (no translation across the stove); the change is orientation/tilt, not movement to a new location.

The pot and its brown liquid remain essentially static; the frothy ring at the liquid's edge and the surface do not show filling, pouring, or a level change, and the mug interior stays empty throughout.
Minor handheld jitter is present: the tile lines and stove grates shift a few pixels frame-to-frame, indicating small camera motion superimposed on the scene, but no deliberate camera pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the mug is about to be filled from the pot or was just emptied; no pouring is visible in this segment.
The state of the stove flame and any heating or boiling before/after the crop.
What the person does with the mug once the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: The exact driver of the mug's tilt (hand rotation vs. slight camera angle change) cannot be separated cleanly; both contribute to the apparent motion.
The liquid's identity and whether visible surface texture changes are due to motion or just lighting/reflection.
Steam or vapor, if any, is not clearly resolvable in these frames.
